artists.biography:
The Lemonheads are an American alternative rock band first formed in 1986 by Evan Dando, Ben Deily and Jesse Peretz. Dando has remained the band's only constant member.

Since its formation, recording and touring lineups of the band have included co-founders Deily and Peretz, John Strohm (Blake Babies), Doug Trachten, Corey Loog Brennan, Byron Hoagland (Folks On Fire), Ben Daughtrey (Squirrel Bait), Juliana Hatfield (Blake Babies), Nic Dalton (Godstar, Sneeze, The Plunderers), Dave Ryan, Patrick "Murph" Murphy (Dinosaur Jr), Bill Gibson (Eastern Dark), Mark 'Budola' Newman, Kenny Lyon, Vess Ruhtenberg, Devon Ashley, Karl Alvarez and Bill Stevenson (Descendents), P. David Hazel and various others.

After their initial punk-influenced releases and tours as an independent/"college rock" band in the late '80s, the Lemonheads' popularity with a mass audience grew in 1992 with the major label album It's a Shame about Ray, which was produced, engineered, and mixed by The Robb Brothers (Bruce Robb, Dee, and Joe). This was followed by a cover of Simon and Garfunkel's "Mrs. Robinson", which eventually became one of the band's most successful singles. The Lemonheads were active until 1997 before going on hiatus, but reformed with a new lineup in 2005 and released The Lemonheads the following year. The band released its latest album, Varshons, in June 2009.

perplexity.description:
Car Button Cloth, released in 1996, is the seventh studio album by The Lemonheads, primarily led by frontman Evan Dando, who performed many instruments alongside drummer Patrick Murphy and various session musicians. The album blends rock and pop elements with a mix of introspective, emotionally raw songs and more accessible, radio-friendly tracks. It features a range of styles from piano-led ballads to jangle-pop, reflecting a period of personal turmoil for Dando, including struggles with addiction and rehabilitation, which influenced the album’s darker lyrical themes.

Musically, Car Button Cloth stands out in The Lemonheads’ discography as a more mature and somber work compared to their earlier, more upbeat releases like It's a Shame About Ray (1992) and Come On Feel the Lemonheads (1993). Despite mixed critical reception at the time of release, with some critics being harsh, the album has since gained a minor cult following among fans who appreciate its emotional depth and Dando’s songwriting growth. Commercially, it reached moderate chart positions, peaking at 130 on the US Billboard 200 and performing better in the UK and Australia. This album was the last studio release by The Lemonheads for a decade, marking the end of their contract with Atlantic Records before Dando pursued solo work.
